# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC's phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> level-3 tasks.
>
> The phase order and acceptance gates in the body of RFC-039 are the sole authority. This document
> is only responsible for decomposing the work into an executable granularity and recording
> conflicts that have not yet been adjudicated.

**Unused numbers (not reclaimed)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`. None of these three
has had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established: the history of this document has zero
matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can verify this), and there
are no repository-wide references. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion). That phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8's numbering is aligned with
its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for individual tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
rationale for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: Every newly registered level-2/level-3 row
**must contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P to which it truly belongs, which may differ
from the containing section) and “**Blocks the mainline**.” `Registered, awaiting scheduling` is no
longer the default state; an unmarked item is deemed **not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique
across the entire document** (tasks on separate tracks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and
must not occupy `N.x`). **Checkoff/completion is recorded by “task id + evidence (gate values, run
id, issue number, file:line),” not by commit number**—`pull --rebase` rewrites local hashes, so
hard-coded numbers inevitably become invalid (2026-10-13 example: `94ad03ce4`→`631eb3e3c`). Look up
commit numbers with `git log`.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” from eight documents into the master table, **five
hard gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been closed:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Resolution                                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps.** RFC-039 defines P5 (checker decomposition) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how to perform the decomposition. The directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one reference to `annotations.rs`, the only mention in the entire batch.                                     | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below).                                                                                                        |
| G2  | **The three `include!` conversion sites have no owner and no implementation.** RFC-039 lists them under P4; `02` assigns them to itself; `06` also lists them under S7. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) does **not** include `semantic_tokens.rs`.                                                                                | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (prerequisite: P4 complete); references in RFC-039 and `06` have been updated to point here. |
| G3  | **Three CI-script inventories coexist.** `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists four scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists four different checks; `04` additionally requires `check-synth-boundary.py`. After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no authoritative inventory**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9. | See §P9 of this document for the unified inventory (11 scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to that table.                             |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`.** `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it and the `Precedence` enum “must be deleted together”; `05` advocates deletion.                                                                                                                             | **Revive in P1; delete with Pratt in P8** (decision C1)—first restore CI coverage, then perform the deletion with the Pratt dead ladder in 8.6.                |
| G5  | **Conflicting wording for the L2 goal.** RFC-039 and this directory's index say “grammar-driven syntax,” whereas `05` self-assesses: “**The implementation does not use true grammar-driven parsing (LALRPOP); it only provides a declarative lookup table.**”                                                                                                      | Consolidated as **fully grammar-driven using LALRPOP** (`05` §Syntax: fully grammar-driven); the G7/G8 acceptance gates enforce that commitment.               |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0  仓库维护机制与代码放置规程     08        ← 新增，先立规矩
P1  复活孤儿测试并修缺陷           06 §S1
P2  建立等价性判据基线             07 全部
P3  修正确性漏洞（最小方案）        02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4  阶段契约与统一 Driver          02
P5  checker 文件内拆分             02 + 本文补齐
P6  类型表示单一化                 03
P7  中间表示 SSA 化                04      } 可并行
P8  前端范式变更                   05      }
P9  防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单）     01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正             06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: The three prohibitions—no invented constructs, no endless filling, and
no patching what should have been refactored—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be
established before work starts; otherwise, reviving tests in P1 would already result in adding `mod`
declarations to `tests/mod.rs`, which is precisely the source of the G4 conflict.

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, user decision 2026-10-11)**: If this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect where the “old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior or resource loss** (crash, stack overflow, silently
> incorrect result)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactoring**, but all four requirements are
> mandatory: ① red first, then green (the red criterion must exist first and genuinely fail); ② do
> not change the externally observable behavior of programs that previously compiled successfully
> and ran correctly (they must not become failures, and existing diagnostic codes / text / exit
> codes must not be removed or changed); ③ register it in the same commit (mark the error type on
> this row + add a phase revision note + fill the “Error Type” line in the PR's required block); ④
> regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible semantics
> / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes still require prior user adjudication.**
> See [07 §Semantic-Correction Routing Criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded criteria
> and A–F whitelist; **“default to a super-refactor and register it afterward” is not accepted**
> (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes and regressions cannot be
> distinguished, which conflicts with both “C5′ does not exist” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

      position is decomposed at the wrong level—`g: () -> ((x: Int) -> Int) = inc` reports E1012 and
      expects `int64` (the annotation was read as **curried**, meaning “one value parameter
      returning Int”), while `g: () -> ((x: Int) -> Int) = () => { return inc }` expects
      `fn(int64)->int64` but finds the **overall** lambda type (`fn() -> fn(int64)->int64`); the two
      paths give **mutually contradictory expectations** for the same annotation, resulting in **no
      valid annotation syntax** for “a function whose return type is itself a function” (removing
      the annotation makes it pass). **The annotation itself parses correctly** (the parser was
      ruled out by measurement). **Owning phase: P3; Blocks the mainline: No** |

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactoring itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by
an ordering constraint**. It is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items”
(narrowing Rust to `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed before P4**: RFC-029g's deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surface of
all four refactoring phases. Reversing the order would require repeating the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / checker layout / SSA IR.

| RFC-029g deletion surface                                           | Files                                                                                                              | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criteria first)**:

1. **Red first, then green**: each of the two behavioral changes must have its red criterion
   committed before code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② an
   unreferenced top-level binding in a Lib/Script role newly reports W1001 (previously `pub` items
   were absolutely exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting `exempt_pub` cases from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and `is_pub` fixtures, equivalent new cases must replace
   them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse errors + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff must be
   explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: It overlaps 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be serial and
cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). RFC-029g does not depend on
3.4; the implementer chooses which to do first based on available context.

|                             | 5.3.2 **Keep `collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) as `pub(crate)` under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 **did not migrate it** in practice ⇒ the “zero consumer changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a new `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is ever migrated with the family (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that this import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 5.3.1        | **Zero consumer changes** is this step's hard acceptance criterion: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty                                                                                               |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is ever migrated with the annotation family, **then** `checker.rs` must add a
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that this import remains unchanged. 5.3 did not
migrate it in practice, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines—this
increases navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and provides zero decoupling benefit. The remaining
submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split when the file grows back to 1,500
lines.

**Hard acceptance criterion** (**2026-10-27 revision, following 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be empty in **every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-driver test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive changed code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be changed when mechanically required, provided each is
registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted and assertions must not
be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-repair** batch (new diagnostic codes +
baseline updates), does not fall under this hard criterion, and is handled as a separate round with
a separate decision.

> **Revision relationship**: The original criterion (2026-10-26 decision ②) read
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-difference requirement to all of
> `tests/`; the revised criterion **changes only direct-driver test files from “zero difference” to
> “changeable but file / line count / reason must be registered”**. The zero-difference requirements
> for the **corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard
> library (`src/std/`)** remain unchanged. First application = 6.1.2: only
> `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed by **3 lines** (two `assert_format_eq` occurrences of
> `i64`→`Int64` + one comment line), because the expected type-name spelling in the assertion had to
> follow the changed spelling; no test was deleted and no assertion was weakened. See 09a “P6 6.1
> Name Canonicalization Closeout” for details.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 emergency stop-loss path (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping correctness vulnerabilities must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x literally adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                             |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and the corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must be **written red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                           |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order would freeze bugs into the stage table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                     |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)'s deletion surface covers P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8's respective rewrite targets (the inventory is in this document §P3.5)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, checker layout, and IR (D56) |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` conversion and checker decomposition modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated, otherwise regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                      |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation                                                                                                                                                       |
| P7/P8 → P9                | 9.5's snapshot baseline and 9.3's `pub(crate)` leakage count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                  |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                      | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC-039)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | The file sets are disjoint: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                |
| B                                          | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| C                                          | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| D                                          | 4.4 (proof-layer finalization) ∥ the entire P6 line                                | 02 explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| E                                          | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| F                                          | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | 9.5's snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| G                                          | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | The file sets are disjoint (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` sites in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; there are no intersections) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same batch); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (already unified into P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (the same files, `checker.rs`
/ `environment.rs`—the external track's `pub`-deletion batch and the silent-channel repair must be
serial).

**New internal documentation constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial;
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial, and 7b's `Phi` arm must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks”; rules are
  “pre-hoc judgment.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching what should have been refactored”; only
  D0–D4's review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative inventory of CI scripts**—the original G3's three coexisting
  inventories prevented convergence. This table merges them, with 11 scripts each owned by one phase
  and an explicit report-only state and hard-conversion point.
- **P3.5 absorbs RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to execute after the
  refactoring”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactoring means repeating the same deletions on a new grammar,
  checker layout, and IR. This is the same lesson as absorbing 7e's `2315`/`2341` and S4's
  RFC-status correction into the WBS.
- **P5's steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker decomposition would exceed the revertible granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero consumer changes” as a hard acceptance criterion**—the decomposition must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (repairing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the repaired
  defects must not be rolled back,” without requiring a record of “what was repaired.” **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x repair commit message must reference the repaired test name and defect
  description, providing evidence for later bisection.
- ~~**7b.1's granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b under
  DoD 6 as two exclusive commits.
- **8.2.1's granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 renamed references; missing one **silently
  changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 lands as 7e.1,
  D20 lands as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation is merged into 7e.1, with the deletion action
  left to P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to an “independent issue”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: absorbed as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core language
  semantics and must not be left as an implementation residual.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into P10
  S6's generation-time gate task.
